title: Microsoft Scales Back Rented AI Cloud Computing Capacity From Oracle
summary:
The company is reducing its lease of AI cloud compute capacity from Oracle after deciding not to renew segments of their rental agreement. Microsoft has begun turning off the rented infrastructure over recent months because the hardware, which relies on older Nvidia chips, no longer meets the company's current technical specifications, Bloomberg reported.

The move is part of a broader reassessment of Microsoft's cloud partnerships and AI infrastructure spending. Oracle shares fell 5% following the report, though Oracle maintains that demand for its AI services remains strong and stated in September that some 4 year old GPU contracts were renewed at a 20% premium.

Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Compute Deal $ORCL $MSFT

Microsoft is scaling back rented AI computing capacity from Oracle after choosing not to renew parts of the agreement. The capacity had become less useful as it relied on older-generation Nvidia chips that no longer matched Microsoft’s specifications, prompting the company to turn off the rented infrastructure over recent months.

The move forms part of a broader reassessment of Microsoft’s cloud partnerships and AI infrastructure spending. Oracle maintains that demand for its AI infrastructure remains strong, including for older GPUs, and said in September that some four-year-old GPU contracts were being renewed at a 20% premium to original pricing.
